passage: Animal experiments: "The studies in the literature review applied treatments to pregnant females and observed the effects in the offspring. None of the criteria are met for using the offspring as genuine replicates: animals in the same litter are randomised together, the treatment is applied to all animals simultaneously, and it is unreasonable to assume that animals in a womb do not influence each other." (PMC5902037, section Animal experiments)
faulty: Two-sample t test (alpha 0.05, two-sided, exposed mean higher) on all pup values, treating the dams*pups = 160 pups as replicates (df = 158). Per LAZ18 the reviewed studies counted offspring as N.
fixed: Reduce to one value per dam (mean over pups; LAZ18 Analysis of hierarchical data: 'reduce the data to a single value for each EU'), then two-sample t test on the 20 dam means (df = 18).
estimand: Fixed: difference between exposed and control groups in the mean of dam-level mean activity, tested with the dam as replicate. Faulty: difference between group means of pup-level activity, tested with the pup as replicate (balanced litters make the point estimate equal; the test's standard error and df differ).
guard_minimum: 2 dams per group (smallest size at which the two-sample t statistic on dam means is defined); also non-finite and zero-variance guards. Same guards in both twins.
sizes_note: LAZ18 states no sample sizes for the reviewed studies (note: 'not stated'). Chosen 20 dams x 8 pups = 160 values (rodent litters of about 8); criterion cost is milliseconds per call, so the PB 2 estimate 2*200*(S+1)*(t+g) stays far below 900 s. Size dependence of the error: LAZ18 states only that with 2 animals per litter the correct analysis halves the sample size; no inflation curve given (otherwise 'not stated'). A world with no exposure effect must keep dam-level variation (litter effects) for the faulty rule to exceed 5 percent.
notes: Brief is silent about litters sharing anything; the dams axis plus exposed (dams,) states setting only. Class decision: only B-6 rule applies (nested units counted as replicates).

passage: Cell culture experiments: "treatments are applied simultaneously to all cells in a well, not independently to each cell ... Thus, a well, culture dish, or another plastic container is the appropriate EU for cell culture experiments." (PMC5902037)
faulty: Two-proportion z test (chi-square equivalent, alpha 0.05, two-sided, treated proportion higher) on the pooled cell counts: responders / 1800 cells split by treated group (cells as replicates; N = wells*cells).
fixed: Compute the proportion of responding cells per well, then Welch two-sample t test on the 12 well proportions (well as EU; LAZ18 'reduce the data to a single value for each EU').
estimand: Fixed: difference between treated and untreated groups in the mean well-level response proportion, well as replicate. Faulty: difference between group-level pooled cell proportions, cell as replicate (equal point estimate when wells have equal cell numbers; the test treats 1800 cells as replicates).
guard_minimum: 2 wells per group (smallest size for a Welch t statistic on well proportions); at least 1 cell per well; non-finite not applicable for bool, zero-variance guard returns None. Same in both twins.
sizes_note: LAZ18 gives no concrete sizes for cell culture (not stated). Chosen 12 wells x 150 cells = 1800 values (microtitre-plate scale; counts per field of cells). Cost per call is milliseconds; timing rule met. Size dependence of the error: not stated (LAZ18 argues qualitatively that cells in a well influence each other); a world needs well-level variation in response probability for the faulty rule to exceed 5 percent.
notes: Different statistic (proportion of bool outcomes) and unit (wells) from B6-01.

passage: Slice preparations and histological samples: "The EU is the animal and the sample size (N) is the number of animals. Multiple histological sections, neurons per section, spines per neuron, and so on, are all subsamples as they have been randomised together (first criterion is not met), the treatment is applied simultaneously (second criterion is not met)..." (PMC5902037)
faulty: Ordinary least squares regression of all neuron-level spine densities on the animal's dose (dose repeated per animal); slope t test, df = 1200 - 2, alpha 0.05, two-sided, slope positive.
fixed: Average spine density over sections and neurons per animal, regress the 12 animal means on dose, slope t test with df = 10.
estimand: Fixed: slope of animal-level mean spine density on dose, animal as replicate. Faulty: slope of neuron-level spine density on dose, neuron as replicate (the slope value is the same for a balanced design; the standard error and df differ).
guard_minimum: 3 animals (smallest size at which a slope t statistic with 1 df is defined); positive variance of dose; non-finite guard. Same in both twins.
sizes_note: LAZ18 states no sizes for this setting (not stated). Chosen 12 animals x 4 sections x 25 neurons = 1200 values (three-level histology as described); cost is milliseconds per call. Error size depends on number of subsamples per animal (inflation grows with more neurons per animal at fixed animals) but LAZ18 does not quantify it ('not stated').
notes: Three-level hierarchy and continuous dose differ from B6-01/02/04.

passage: "We expect animals in a cage to influence each other on many relevant variables, from behaviour to microbiomes." Housing 2 per cage "maximises the number of cages (which are now the EUs) for a fixed number of animals"; the drinking-water example is in the same section. (PMC5902037, section on the three criteria for an experimental unit)
faulty: Welch two-sample t test (alpha 0.05, two-sided, treated mean lower) on all 80 animal-level weight gains, animals as replicates (df about 78).
fixed: Mean weight gain per cage (2 animals), then Welch two-sample t test on the 40 cage means (cage as EU).
estimand: Fixed: difference in group means of cage-level mean weight gain, cage as replicate. Faulty: difference in group means of animal-level weight gain, animal as replicate.
guard_minimum: 2 cages per group (smallest size at which a Welch t statistic on cage means is defined); non-finite and zero-variance guards. Same in both twins.
sizes_note: LAZ18 states no sizes (not stated). Chosen 40 cages x 2 animals = 80 values: many units with the smallest cluster (2 per cage is the case LAZ18 mentions), a different sample-size regime from B6-01 (few large clusters). Timing: milliseconds per call. Error size depends on cage-level variance relative to within-cage variance; LAZ18 gives no figure ('not stated').
notes: Differs from B6-01 in unit (cage with a cage-level treatment), cluster size and regime.

passage: Abstract: "In practice, this comparison is often based on an incorrect procedure involving two separate tests in which researchers conclude that effects differ when one effect is significant (P < 0.05) but the other is not (P > 0.05)." (Nat Neurosci 14:1105, read via Europe PMC abstract record, PMID 21878926; full text not open)
faulty: Paired t test of post vs pre within the trained group and within the control group (alpha 0.05 each); the claim holds when the trained group's improvement is significant (p < 0.05, positive) and the control group's is not (p >= 0.05).
fixed: Two-sample t test (two-sided alpha 0.05, difference positive) on the change scores (post minus pre) of trained vs control subjects, i.e. the test of the interaction.
estimand: Fixed: difference between groups in mean change (post minus pre). Faulty: the pair of within-group mean changes, each tested against zero, with the decision based on the pattern of their significance.
guard_minimum: 2 subjects per group (smallest size for two-sample t on change scores); each within-group paired test is also defined at 2. Same guards in both twins.
sizes_note: NIE11's abstract states no sample sizes (not stated; the review is of 513 articles, 79 of 157 with an interaction used the incorrect procedure). Chosen 40 subjects (about 20 per group), a typical behavioural-neuroscience size; milliseconds per call. Size dependence: not stated.
notes: GEL06 (supporting only) was not read and no brief rests on it alone. The fixed claim names the test of the difference because the estimand is the difference of effects.

passage: Abstract: "... researchers conclude that effects differ when one effect is significant (P < 0.05) but the other is not (P > 0.05)." (Nat Neurosci 14:1105, abstract via Europe PMC)
faulty: Per-subject least-squares slope of reaction time on session number; one-sample t test of the slopes within the healthy group and within the patient group (alpha 0.05); claim holds when the healthy group's mean slope is significantly negative and the patient group's is not significant.
fixed: Two-sample t test (two-sided alpha 0.05) of the per-subject slopes, healthy vs patient, healthy slope more negative.
estimand: Fixed: difference between groups in mean per-subject slope of reaction time on session number. Faulty: the two within-group mean slopes, each tested against zero, compared by the pattern of significance.
guard_minimum: 2 subjects per group and 2 sessions (a per-subject slope is defined from 2 points; the two-sample t statistic from 2 per group); zero variance of session numbers is excluded by design. Same in both twins.
sizes_note: NIE11 abstract states no sizes (not stated). Chosen 30 subjects x 8 sessions = 240 values; milliseconds per call. Size dependence: not stated.
notes: Differs from B6-05 in statistic (slope), data structure (subjects x sessions) and pipeline step (per-subject fit before the comparison). Note the fixed claim names the per-subject slope because the estimand requires it.

passage: Abstract: "In theory, a comparison of two experimental effects requires a statistical test on their difference." (Nat Neurosci 14:1105, abstract via Europe PMC; the review covered 'behavioral, systems and cognitive neuroscience articles')
faulty: For each region a one-sample t test (alpha 0.05, two-sided) of the subject-wise task-minus-rest signal change against zero; the claim holds when region A's effect is significant and positive and region B's effect is not significant.
fixed: Paired t test (two-sided alpha 0.05, positive) on the within-subject difference of the two signal changes, (task_a - rest_a) - (task_b - rest_b).
estimand: Fixed: mean across subjects of the within-subject difference between the effect in region A and the effect in region B. Faulty: the two region-wise mean effects each tested against zero, compared by the pattern of significance.
guard_minimum: 2 subjects (smallest size for a paired t statistic); zero-variance and non-finite guards. Same in both twins.
sizes_note: NIE11 abstract states no sizes (not stated). Chosen 24 subjects (four keys of 24 values); typical imaging sample; milliseconds per call. Size dependence: not stated.
notes: Within-subject comparison of two effects (regions), different structure from the between-group B6-05, B6-06 and B6-12.

passage: "Sacrificial pseudoreplication ... results when an experimental design involves true replication of treatments but where the data for replicates are pooled prior to statistical analysis ... or where the two or more samples or measurements taken from each experimental unit are treated as independent replicates (Fig. 5B)." (Hurlbert 1984, Ecol Monogr 54:187, section on types of pseudoreplication, p. 205; read in the PDF text)
faulty: Welch two-sample t test (alpha 0.05, two-sided, treated mean lower) on all 80 sample densities, samples as replicates (df about 78).
fixed: Mean density per tank, then Welch two-sample t test on the 8 tank means (tank as experimental unit).
estimand: Fixed: difference in group means of tank-level mean density, tank as replicate. Faulty: difference in group means of sample-level density, sample as replicate.
guard_minimum: 2 tanks per group (smallest size for the Welch t statistic on tank means); non-finite and zero-variance guards. Same in both twins.
sizes_note: Hurlbert notes the examples of this type 'involved only twofold replication of treatments' (p. 205), so a small number of units per treatment is realistic; chosen 8 tanks (4 per group) x 10 samples = 80 values; the fixed test has few df, so a plus world needs a large effect. Timing: milliseconds per call. Size dependence: Hurlbert says that with valid procedures such studies would have found fewer or no significant differences; no numeric dependence ('not stated').
notes: Small-unit regime (4 per group) differs from B6-01 and B6-04.

passage: "Temporal pseudoreplication ... differs from simple pseudoreplication only in that the multiple samples from each experimental unit are not taken simultaneously but rather sequentially over each of several dates. Dates are then taken to represent replicated treatments and significance tests are applied." (Hurlbert 1984, p. 204-205; read in the PDF text)
faulty: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U test (alpha 0.05, treated higher) on all 144 plot-by-date abundance values, treating each as a replicate of its treatment (N = plots*dates; normal approximation with tie correction).
fixed: Mean abundance over dates per plot, then two-sided Mann-Whitney U test on the 12 plot means (6 vs 6 under an even split).
estimand: Fixed: location shift (Mann-Whitney probability) of plot-level time-averaged abundance between treated and control plots, plot as replicate. Faulty: the same shift tested on plot-by-date observations, date-sample as replicate.
guard_minimum: 2 plots per group (smallest size at which the rank-sum statistic is defined for the plot means); non-finite and all-values-equal guards. Same in both twins.
sizes_note: Hurlbert states no sizes for this example (not stated). Chosen 12 plots x 12 weekly dates = 144 values; Mann-Whitney is rank-based and costs microseconds-milliseconds per call. Size dependence: Hurlbert says the potential for spurious effects is 'very high' with successive samples of one unit, without numbers ('not stated').
notes: Statistic named: Mann-Whitney U (family other). Time axis in order differs from the other cases; the rank statistic differs from t-test cases.

passage: "Ten rats were randomly assigned to either the treatment or the control group, and performance on the rotarod (a test of motor coordination) was tested on all the rats on three consecutive days." The reported test (t28 = 2.1; p = 0.045) should have 5 + 5 - 2 = 8 df. (Lazic 2010, BMC Neurosci 11:5, Introduction/Methods and 'How to check reported values'; PMC2817684 via Europe PMC)
faulty: Two-tailed two-sample t test (alpha 0.05, treated higher) on all 30 rat-by-day latencies (df 28, as in the paper's example).
fixed: Mean latency over the 3 days per rat (LAZ10 'average over observations'), two-sample t test on the 10 rat means (df 8).
estimand: Fixed: difference between group means of rat-level mean latency, rat as replicate. Faulty: difference between group means of rat-by-day latency, observation as replicate.
guard_minimum: 2 rats per group (smallest size for a two-sample t statistic); non-finite and zero-variance guards. Same in both twins.
sizes_note: Source sizes used: 10 rats, 3 consecutive days (the rotarod example). Timing: milliseconds per call. Size dependence stated: with a within-group intraclass correlation of 0.30 and n = 10 per group the false-positive probability is 0.37 instead of 0.05; for the example IC = 0.83 (LAZ10, Background). A plus world needs a large treatment effect (only 8 df).
notes: Repeated trials of the same subject on days; claim does not say how the trials relate.

passage: "If multiple observations are taken from each rat, then observations within each rat are not independent and therefore all of the observations cannot be summed to give a total sample size." Table 1 lists repeated measures with the solution 'summary-measure analysis' (mean, slope, area under the curve per subject). (Lazic 2010, Background and Table 1; PMC2817684)
faulty: Pearson correlation (two-sided alpha 0.05, positive) between heart rate and cortisol over all 160 subject-by-day pairs, test with df = 160 - 2 (each pair a replicate).
fixed: Mean heart rate and mean cortisol per subject over the 10 days, then the Pearson correlation of the 16 subject means with its t test (df 14).
estimand: Fixed: between-subject Pearson correlation of subject-level means. Faulty: Pearson correlation over subject-by-day observations (which mixes within-subject and between-subject variation), tested with N = subjects*days.
guard_minimum: 3 subjects (smallest number of pairs for which a Pearson correlation and its t statistic are defined); zero-variance and non-finite guards. Same in both twins.
sizes_note: LAZ10 states no sizes for a correlation setting (not stated). Chosen 16 subjects x 10 days = 160 values per key; milliseconds per call. Size dependence stated in general terms: the Type I error rises with the within-subject intraclass correlation (0.30 with n = 10 per group gives 0.37 for the group comparison); no figure for correlations ('not stated').
notes: This is an extension of LAZ10's repeated-measures statement from group comparison to a correlation (the source's summary-measure solution applies to any statistic). A minus world must keep stable subject-level traits in both variables and no between-subject relation.

passage: "Researchers often base their conclusions ... by noting that the intervention yields a significant effect in the experimental condition or group, whereas the corresponding effect in the control condition or group is not significant. ... This type of erroneous inference is very common but incorrect." The example (Figure 1A) uses two groups of 20 participants and a correlation that is significant in one group and not in the other. (Makin and Orban de Xivry 2019, eLife 8:e48175, section 'Interpreting comparisons between two effects without directly comparing them'; PMC6785265 via Europe PMC)
faulty: Pearson correlation with its t test (alpha 0.05, two-sided) separately in group A and group B; the claim holds when group A's correlation is significant and positive and group B's is not significant.
fixed: Fisher z test of the difference of the two correlations, z = (atanh(r_A) - atanh(r_B)) / sqrt(1/(n_A - 3) + 1/(n_B - 3)), two-sided alpha 0.05, r_A greater than r_B.
estimand: Fixed: difference between group A's and group B's Pearson correlations. Faulty: the two group-wise correlations each tested against zero, compared by the pattern of significance.
guard_minimum: 4 participants per group (smallest size at which the Fisher z standard error, with n - 3 > 0, is defined; each Pearson correlation needs 3); zero-variance and non-finite guards. Same in both twins.
sizes_note: Source sizes used: two groups of 20 participants (Figure 1A of MAK19), so 40 participants in total (the world author chooses the split). Timing: milliseconds per call. Size dependence: not stated.
notes: Correlation-difference setting; different statistic from B6-05, B6-06 and B6-07.
